extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of art and architectural history; educated general public interested in Venice and aesthetics
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria for judging painting and architecture (especially Venetian) in relation to religion, politics, and cultural origins; oriented toward historical and aesthetic analysis rather than technical construction guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts as evidence of political and moral condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence which I shall be able to deduce from the arts of Venice will be both frequent and irrefragable, that the decline of her political prosperity was exactly coincident with that of domestic and individual religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the production and character of the arts (painting, architecture, etc.) as direct, repeatable testimony to the broader political and moral state of a people. Correlate stylistic and thematic changes in art with historical markers of political decline or vigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private religious vitality vs public deadness
rubrics_metrics.description: The most curious phenomenon in all Venetian history is the vitality of religion in private life, and its deadness in public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a society's culture, distinguish between private, domestic religious feeling (which may be sincere and life-giving) and the formal public observances that may be hollow. Artistic evidence that shows sincere private devotion (humble domestic imagery, personal piety in portraits, private chapels) indicates one condition; grand public ritual without heartfelt substance indicates another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial motive as defining national action
rubrics_metrics.description: That spring was her commercial interest,—this the one motive of all her important political acts, or enduring national animosities. She... calculated the glory of her conquests by their value, and estimated their justice by their facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate political and artistic decisions in Venice by considering commercial incentives as primary motives. If artworks, monuments, or state commissions prioritize mercantile display or value over spiritual or civic meaning, treat that as evidence of commerce-driven policy rather than religious or moral purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of individuals measured by training and self-mastery
rubrics_metrics.description: The real question is... how they were trained; how they were made masters of themselves, servants of their country, patient of distress, impatient of dishonor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing historical figures (patrons, artists, statesmen) focus on formative practices, training, and demonstrated character rather than rank or title. Artistic/historical narratives that show cultivation of self-command and civic service are indicators of true moral heroism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious temper in painting as criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The most solemn spirit of religious faith animates [Bellini's] works to the last. There is no religion in any work of Titian's: there is not even the smallest evidence of religious temper or sympathies either in himself, or in those for whom he painted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge paintings (especially sacred subjects) by whether a 'religious temper' animates them — authenticity of devotional feeling versus mere formal or decorative treatment. Use comparative analysis (e.g., Bellini vs Titian) to reveal whether a painter's work embodies sincere piety or merely employs religious subject matter for rhetorical/coloristic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordination of sacred subject to decoration/portraiture is negative
rubrics_metrics.description: His larger sacred subjects are merely themes for the exhibition of pictorial rhetoric,—composition and color. His minor works are generally made subordinate to purposes of portraiture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat artworks that subordinate religious narrative to compositional display or portraiture (i.e., where the sacred theme is a pretext for showing technique, color, or flattering individual likenesses) as symptomatic of decline in religious sincerity. Use examples (Titian's Madonna in the Frari linked to Pesaro portraits) as anti-patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist's early education shapes religious/artistic feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: This is not merely because John Bellini was a religious man and Titian was not. Titian and Bellini are each true representatives of the school of painters contemporary with them; and the difference in their artistic feeling is a consequence not so much of difference in their own natural characters as in their early education: Bellini was brought up in faith; Titian in formalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attributing stylistic or spiritual differences among artists, consider formative influences and education (religious upbringing vs formal secular training) as decisive factors. Use biographical/educational context to explain aesthetic differences rather than only innate temperament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture as expression of religious condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Each architecture express[es] a condition of religion; each an erroneous condition, yet necessary to the correction of the others, and corrected by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate architectural styles not merely by structural or decorative criteria but as embodiments of religious/spiritual conditions of their cultures. Identify how formal architectural choices (orders, ornamentation, spatial organization) reflect theological or ritual priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation-from-Greece-through-Rome-and-the-East diagnostic
rubrics_metrics.description: All European architecture, bad and good, old and new, is derived from Greece through Rome, and colored and perfected from the East. The history of architecture is nothing but the tracing of the various modes and directions of this derivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use genealogical tracing of forms (Greek shaft, Roman arch, Eastern foliations) as a primary method to classify and assess European architectural works. Map features back to their cultural sources to judge authenticity, continuity, or degeneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two real orders (Doric and Corinthian) as foundational standard
rubrics_metrics.description: There are only two real orders, and there never can be any more until doomsday... On one of these orders the ornament is convex: those are Doric, Norman... On the other the ornament is concave: those are Corinthian, Early English, Decorated...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing ornament and order, use the Doric/Corinthian dichotomy as the root taxonomy; treat other 'orders' as variants or derivations. This serves as a baseline for judging correctness or degeneration of subsequent stylistic inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vitality of architecture depends on vigor and purity of its animating religion
rubrics_metrics.description: That art... being, in points of main importance, the same; that is to say, both of them a true continuance and sequence of the art of old Rome itself... dependent for all its power on the vigor and freshness of the religion which animated it; and as that vigor and purity departed, losing its own vitality, and sinking into nerveless rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether an architectural style is alive or formalistic by determining the health of the religious or cultural impulse behind it. Stagnation, over-decoration without purpose, or 'nerveless rest' indicate diminished spiritual impetus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and read the three constituent elements (Roman, Lombard, Arab)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ducal palace of Venice contains the three elements in exactly equal proportions — the Roman, Lombard, and Arab. It is the central building of the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze complex buildings as syntheses: identify Roman (round-arched, classical shafts, mosaic imagery), Lombard/Northern (grouped and vaulting shafts, robust anatomy, active figurative sculpture), and Arab (pointed/foliated arches, arabesque ornament, horizontal color-banding, domes/minarets) contributions. Use such elemental reading to understand a building's cultural meaning and historical position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architectural features as diagnostic signs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Christian Roman and Byzantine work is round-arched, with single and well-proportioned shafts; capitals imitated from classical Roman; mouldings more or less so; and large surfaces of walls entirely covered with imagery, mosaic, and paintings... The Arab school... points the arch and writhes it into extravagant foliations... bars his surfaces with horizontal lines of color... He retains the dome, and adds the minaret... The whole body of the Northern architecture... may be described as rough but majestic work, round-arched, with grouped shafts, added vaulting shafts, and endless imagery of active life and fantastic superstitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying and evaluating regional styles, use concrete morphological markers (arch shape, shaft grouping, capital types, surface treatment, ornament disposition) to assign lineage and judge aesthetic success. These features function as readable signs of cultural influence and of relative refinement, strength, or spirituality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dating stylistic change to sociocultural shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: I put the commencement of the Fall of Venice as far back as 1418... John Bellini was born in 1423, and Titian in 1480... Between the years of their births the vital religion of Venice had expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link chronological appearance of artists/styles to wider social and religious transformations. Use birthdates, commissions, and the emergence of certain decorative tendencies (e.g., increasing formalism) as indices of cultural change; treat rapid stylistic shifts as evidence of underlying sociopolitical or spiritual transitions.
